story.speaker: Axiom
story.message: Welcome, young thinker. Machine learning is teaching computers to learn from examples.

story.speaker: Axiom
story.message: Instead of writing exact rules, we show the computer many examples and let it find the pattern.

story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: It's a bit like how you learned to recognize cats after seeing many pictures of them!

concept.title: Learning from examples
concept.explanation: Machine learning lets a computer find patterns by studying many examples, instead of being told exact rules.
concept.example: Show 100 photos labeled 'cat' or 'dog' -> the computer learns to tell them apart.

playground.instructions: Look at the shape examples and guess the rule the computer might learn.

options: Following exact rules a programmer writes for every case

story.speaker: Axiom
story.message: Pattern recognition is the heart of machine learning.

story.speaker: Axiom
story.message: Look at these shapes — can you tell what comes next in the sequence?

story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: Your brain just did what an ML model tries to do!

concept.title: Pattern recognition
concept.explanation: Pattern recognition means noticing a repeating rule in data, so you can predict what comes next.

playground.instructions: Study the shape sequence and pick what should come next.

challenge.prompt: Sequence: Red, Blue, Red, Blue, ___. What comes next?

story.speaker: Axiom
story.message: Classification means sorting things into the correct group, like 'cat' or 'dog'.

story.speaker: Axiom
story.message: A well-trained model looks at features — size, shape, color — to decide the group.

story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: You classify things every day without even noticing!

concept.title: Classification
concept.explanation: Classification is sorting an example into one of several known groups based on its features.

playground.instructions: Drag each animal card into the group it belongs to.

challenge.prompt: Match each feature set to the correct animal group.

story.speaker: Axiom
story.message: Models learn from training data, but we must test them on examples they've never seen.

story.speaker: Axiom
story.message: If a model only memorizes the training set, it won't work well on new data.

story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: It's like studying with practice questions, then taking a different real test!

concept.title: Training vs. testing
concept.explanation: We split examples into a training set (to learn from) and a test set (to check if the model really learned the pattern, not just memorized it).
concept.example: 80 photos to train the model, 20 new photos to test if it really learned.

playground.instructions: Drag examples into the training pile or the testing pile and see how the split changes.

challenge.prompt: Why do we test a model on examples it has never seen?
options: To check if it truly learned the pattern, not just memorized

story.speaker: Axiom
story.message: You've learned patterns, classification, and training versus testing. Now build your own!

story.speaker: Axiom
story.message: A classifier learns from labeled training examples, then predicts the label for new ones.

story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: This is the Boss Challenge — train and test a tiny classifier!

concept.title: Building a classifier
concept.explanation: To build a classifier: gather labeled examples, split them into training and test sets, train the model on the training set, then check its accuracy on the test set.
concept.example: Label 20 fruits as 'apple' or 'banana' -> train on 16 -> test on the other 4.

playground.instructions: Label the fruit examples, split them into train/test, then see how well your classifier predicts the test set.

challenge.prompt: Put the steps of building a classifier in the correct order.
correctOrder: Split into training and test sets
